newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares shaky but well supported.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares shaky but well supported.

text.p: Belgian shares were slightly weaker in early business on Thursday but dealers were confident that the market remained well underpinned and would edge further up to new record highs in the run-up to the summer.

"There are no major risks," said Pieter Vander Stichele at Generale Bank. He said that the EU summit in Amsterdam on June 16-17 was also no threat to markets as member states were showing plenty of willingness to clinch a deal.
Vander Stichele added that shares were not only permanently lifted by low interest rates and the dollar but even more so by the lack of lucrative alternatives for stocks.
At 0855 GMT, the Bel-20 index was down 0.13 percent or 3.00 points, at 2,281.40. "People want shares, it's real asset inflation," Vander Stichele said.
The outcome of the French elections and new French government line-up had no influence on Belgian shares, he said.
About one billion francs worth of Belgian shares were traded after one hour of trade with utility firm Electrabel market leader in value terms amid talk of a possible merger with Tractebel.
But dealers feared such a merger would hurt the share price of the companies, both units of holding firm SGB.
Electrabel was down 1.4 percent at 7,680 francs, making it one of the biggest forward market losers.

Generale Bank earlier said in its daily equity focus it was maintaining its buy recommendations for Electrabel for now but could reduce it if the merger would become effective. SGB said on Thursday however that a merger could be years away.
Dealers said a merger would put both shares under persistent selling pressure as many investors would have to cut their positions.
Tractebel was still unaffected though and was up 0.3 percent at 15,575. -- Bert Lauwers, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6815
